dedupe_keys.name: agent based model of a circular food packaging ecosystem to assess packaging waste dynamics dutch beverage packaging comses

description: This agent-based model explores whether circular ecosystems can reduce packaging waste, using the Dutch food and beverage packaging ecosystem as a case study. It contains three agent types that can form closed-loop recycling systems: beverage producers in five packaging formats (cans, PET bottles, glass bottles, cartons and bag-in-boxes), each with packaging demand by volume, weight and reuse potential; packaging producers that make packaging from recycled or virgin material under monopolistic or competitive markets; and waste treaters that collect and recycle packaging waste. Agents choose suppliers each year using bargaining, which seeks the lowest price, or problem-solving, which prioritises recycled content, so the model shows how decision styles, material prices and technology shape recycling rates and waste. Coverage is the Netherlands, as a stylised ecosystem. The code, version 1.0.0 from October 2024, is free to download from the CoMSES Computational Model Library under the MIT licence. Caveats: it is a thesis-scale research model whose parameters are simplified, and it has not been published in a peer-reviewed journal. Simulation uses: testing policies such as recycled-content requirements or deposit schemes on packaging waste flows and recycling capacity. Related records: the SWEET waste emissions tool (model-sweet-solid-waste-emissions-estimation-tool) estimates emissions from municipal waste systems and the EPA recycling infrastructure map (data-epa-recycling-infrastructure-market-opportunities-map) shows recycling facilities.
